title: Truth in Lending (Regulation Z)
summary: The Board and the Bureau (collectively, Agencies) are publishing final rules amending the official interpretations for the Agencies' regulations that implement the Truth in Lending Act (TILA). The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (Dodd- Frank Act) amended TILA to require that the dollar threshold for exempt consumer credit transactions be adjusted annually by the annual percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W). Based on the annual percentage increase in the CPI-W as of June 1, 2026, the exemption threshold will increase from $73,400 to $76,300 effective January 1, 2027. Because the Dodd- Frank Act also requires similar adjustments in the Consumer Leasing Act's threshold for exempt consumer leases, the Agencies are making similar amendments to each of their respective regulations implementing the Consumer Leasing Act elsewhere in the Rules section of this issue of the Federal Register.

title: Consumer Leasing (Regulation M)
summary: The Board and the Bureau (collectively, Agencies) are finalizing amendments to the official interpretations for the Agencies' regulations that implement the Consumer Leasing Act (CLA). The Dodd- Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (Dodd-Frank Act) amended the CLA to require that the dollar threshold for exempt consumer leases be adjusted annually by the annual percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W). Based on the annual percentage increase in the CPI-W as of June 1, 2026, the exemption threshold will increase from $73,400 to $76,300, effective January 1, 2027. Because the Dodd-Frank Act also requires similar adjustments in the Truth in Lending Act's threshold for exempt consumer credit transactions, the Agencies are making similar amendments to each of their respective regulations implementing the Truth in Lending Act elsewhere in the Rules section of this issue of the Federal Register.

title: Appraisals for Higher-Priced Mortgage Loans Exemption Threshold
summary: The OCC, the Board, and the Bureau are finalizing amendments to the official interpretations for their regulations that implement section 129H of the Truth in Lending Act (TILA). Section 129H of TILA establishes special appraisal requirements for "higher-risk mortgages," termed "higher-priced mortgage loans" or "HPMLs" in the agencies' regulations. The regulations provide that transactions of $25,000 or less are exempt from these requirements, adjusted annually based on any annual percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W). Based on the CPI-W in effect as of June 1, 2026, the exemption threshold will increase from $34,200 to $35,500, effective January 1, 2027.

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status for Streaked Horned Lark With a Section 4(d) Rule
summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the streaked horned lark (Eremophila alpestris strigata), a subspecies of grassland songbird from Oregon and Washington, as a threatened species with protective regulations under section 4(d) of the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would maintain the species as a threatened species on the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and continue to extend the Act's protections to the species.

title: Magnuson-Stevens Act Provisions; Fisheries Off West Coast States; Pacific Coast Groundfish Fishery; Pacific Coast Groundfish Fishery Management Plan; Amendment 38; 2027-28 Biennial Specifications and Management Measures
summary: This rule implements 2027-28 harvest specifications and management measures for groundfish caught in the U.S. exclusive economic zone (EEZ) seaward of Washington, Oregon, and California, consistent with the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (MSA) and the Pacific Coast Groundfish Fishery Management Plan (Groundfish FMP). This rule also includes regulations to implement amendment 38 to the Groundfish FMP, which removes rebuilding plan requirements for yelloweye rockfish and California quillback rockfish. Lastly, this rule includes regulations that modify select fishery closures that apply to both groundfish and Pacific halibut.

title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Gulf of Alaska; 2027 and 2028 Harvest Specifications for Groundfish
summary: NMFS proposes 2027 and 2028 harvest specifications, apportionments, and Pacific halibut prohibited species catch (PSC) limits for the groundfish fishery of the Gulf of Alaska (GOA). This action is necessary to establish harvest limits for groundfish during the 2027 and 2028 fishing years and to accomplish the goals and objectives of the Fishery Management Plan for the Groundfish fisheries of the Gulf of Alaska (FMP). The 2027 harvest specifications supersede those previously set in the final 2026 and 2027 harvest specifications, and the 2028 harvest specifications will be superseded in early 2028 when the final 2028 and 2029 harvest specifications are published. The intended effect of this action is to conserve and manage the groundfish resources in the GOA in accordance with the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (Magnuson-Stevens Act).

Request for Comments Concerning Proposed Modification of Section 301 Action on Brazil's Acts, Policies, and Practices Related to Digital Trade and Electronic Payment Services; Unfair, Preferential Tariffs; Anti-Corruption Enforcement; Intellectual Property Protection; Ethanol Market Access; and Illegal Deforestation
summary: The United States Trade Representative (Trade Representative) proposes a modification of the tariff action taken in connection with the Section 301 investigation of Brazil's acts, policies, and practices related to digital trade and electronic payment services; unfair, preferential tariffs; anti-corruption enforcement; intellectual property protection; ethanol market access; and illegal deforestation. Brazil has made insufficient progress in eliminating the acts, policies, and practices USTR identified as actionable. The proposed modification to duties on certain sugar products and finished aircraft seeks to create additional leverage to encourage Brazil to eliminate its acts, policies, and practices identified as actionable in the investigation. USTR is seeking public comment and will hold a public hearing regarding this proposed modification.

Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status With a Section 4(d) Rule for Blanding's Turtle
summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Blanding's turtle (Emydoidea blandingii), a reptile species from 14 States in the midwestern and eastern regions of the United States and 3 Provinces in eastern Canada, as a threatened species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the Blanding's turtle. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. We find that designating critical habitat for this species is not prudent.

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status With Section 4(d) Rule for the Cascade and Columbia Torrent Salamanders
summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Cascade torrent salamander (Rhyacotriton cascadae), a species endemic to the western slope of the Cascade Range in Washington and Oregon, and the Columbia torrent salamander (Rhyacotriton kezeri), a species endemic to the Coast Range in Washington and Oregon, as threatened species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the Cascade torrent salamander and the Columbia torrent salamander. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing these species is warranted. Accordingly, we propose to list the Cascade torrent salamander and Columbia torrent salamander as threatened species with a rule issued under section 4(d) of the Act ("4(d) rule"). If finalized as proposed, this rulemaking action would add these species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the two species. We find that designating critical habitat for this species is not determinable at this time.

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status With Section 4(d) Rule for Ferris's Copper
summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Ferris's copper (Lycaena ferrisi), a butterfly species from Arizona, as a threatened species with protective regulations under section 4(d) of the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12- month finding on a petition to list the Ferris's copper. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. We find that designating critical habitat for this species is not prudent.

title: Standard Instrument Approach Procedures, and Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure Procedures; Miscellaneous Amendments
summary: This rule amends, suspends, or removes Standard Instrument Approach Procedures (SIAPs) and associated Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure Procedures for operations at certain airports. These regulatory actions are needed because of the adoption of new or revised criteria, or because of changes occurring in the National Airspace System, such as the commissioning of new navigational facilities, adding new obstacles, or changing air traffic requirements. These changes are designed to provide for the safe and efficient use of the navigable airspace and to promote safe flight operations under instrument flight rules at the affected airports.

title: Standard Instrument Approach Procedures, and Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure Procedures; Miscellaneous Amendments
summary: This rule establishes, amends, suspends, or removes Standard Instrument Approach Procedures (SIAPS) and associated Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure procedures (ODPs) for operations at certain airports. These regulatory actions are needed because of the adoption of new or revised criteria, or because of changes occurring in the National Airspace System, such as the commissioning of new navigational facilities, adding new obstacles, or changing air traffic requirements. These changes are designed to provide safe and efficient use of the navigable airspace and to promote safe flight operations under instrument flight rules at the affected airports.

title: Data Reporting Requirements for Certain Event Contracts
summary: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission ("Commission" or "CFTC") is finalizing revisions to the Commission's regulations that set forth an alternate framework for reporting of data for certain fully collateralized event contracts (the "Final Rule"). These revisions require certain reporting markets, futures commission merchants, clearing members, and foreign brokers to report certain event contracts pursuant to the regulations in parts 15 through 18 rather than the reporting regulations contained in certain sections of parts 38, 39, 43 and 45.
